topic: Claims weaker than, or covering part of, a canonical policy
evidence: CALIBRATION FG-L1-676a924034 (version-selection part of DEP-003 only), FG-M-1b283f6602 (PST-008 review vs update)
problem: Task section 2 defines CANONICAL_ONLY as entailed 'at the same strength, conditions, exceptions, scope and behavior', but provides no label for an entailed claim that is weaker or narrower than its policy (no remainder, so not CANONICAL_PLUS_DELTA; not EXTRA).
interim_handling: Classified CANONICAL_ONLY when the full-entailment test passes; weakening recorded as strength_vs_canonical=WEAKER and/or coverage PARTIAL (~), which feeds POLICY_COVERAGE PARTIAL_EVIDENCE. Stronger claims are never CANONICAL_ONLY.
a1_update: The M review rejected treating weaker claims as equivalent. The CANONICAL_ONLY label is kept because the fixed label set has no alternative, but every such record now carries normative_strength_equivalence=WEAKER_THAN_CANONICAL, reports separate it, and STRENGTH_DIVERGENCES.jsonl preserves it for Step 3.

topic: Oracle DEFAULT strength does not define deviation mechanics
evidence: CALIBRATION FG-M-eed95edecb, FG-L0-1927451833, FG-K0-4ee4aebfc8 vs FG-K1-d65d888216
problem: Candidates define 'default' as 'deviation needs a concrete reason and must be reported/documented'; the oracle marks policies DEFAULT without stating whether deviations must be reported. Whether a documentation/reporting duty is entailed therefore depends on an undefined oracle semantic.
interim_handling: A per-rule or general documentation/reporting duty for deviations is a non-entailed workflow remainder (CANONICAL_PLUS_DELTA k=W or EXTRA_WORKFLOW), confidence at most MEDIUM.

topic: Host semantics of hook registration fields are not executed
evidence: CALIBRATION FG-L0-29b2fd6409, FG-M1-6a4037ede3, AUG1-FX-CIS-M-0002-a; all six candidates' settings.json use exec-form args and onFailure
problem: Whether Claude Code honours 'args' exec form, 'onFailure: block', PostToolUseFailure payloads and decision:block exactly as the candidates assume was not tested; the effective runtime behavior of fail-closed gating cannot be established statically.
interim_handling: Classify by declared/implemented intent; never assert runtime effect; flag records whose classification depends solely on such host support (review_needed, confidence <= MEDIUM).

topic: Normativity of declarative technique in knowledge skills
evidence: CALIBRATION FG-K1-924db7529d (ef-core technique), FG-L0-7650a991ec (WAF exposure step), FG-L0-c79ad13875 (example code)
problem: Candidates declare knowledge skills to hold 'technique and examples only' (e.g. M MAP.md:22-26), while much skill text is phrased as directives. The task requires actual normative meaning; the oracle excludes 'optional technique'. The boundary between prescriptive technique and illustration is a reviewer judgment.
interim_handling: Prescriptive technique is normative at its stated/implied strength (often DEFAULT/SHOULD) and classified by the entailment test; explicitly illustrative content is NON_NORMATIVE; copy risk is noted, not converted into a rule.

topic: Domain of approval gates and CI pipeline content
evidence: CALIBRATION FG-K0-2d15df1383 (reference-graph Reserved), FG-K1-5383f42e9b (no automatic package upgrades in CI)
problem: The domain list does not say whether an approval gate on product architecture, or the content of CI/CD definitions, is PRODUCT_ENGINEERING or WORKFLOW_ENFORCEMENT.
interim_handling: Approval gates whose object is product architecture/technology and CI/CD pipeline content are PRODUCT_ENGINEERING; the agent's procedure and the hooks/checkers acting on its work are WORKFLOW_ENFORCEMENT.

topic: Directional preference wording versus non-normative text
evidence: FG-M-d0b6a09cce: ef-core SKILL.md:388-389 "generated migration scripts are often preferable"
problem: C5 lists "useful" and "can" as non-normative but does not address hedged directional preferences; the first classification treated "often preferable" as NON_NORMATIVE, inconsistent with other prefer statements.
interim_handling: Directional comparative wording is a normative preference at SHOULD/DEFAULT; the hedge lowers confidence. Text stating no direction stays NON_NORMATIVE.

topic: Semantic coverage and normative-strength equivalence are separate axes
evidence: M: 32 CANONICAL_ONLY records marked WEAKER; a mechanical audit found a further 66 stronger and 45 weaker CO links marked SAME
problem: strength_vs_canonical defaulted to SAME without comparing the record modality with the policy tag, so the distinction was not reliably preserved.
interim_handling: Mechanical strength_links on every link; each mismatch needs a reviewer resolution; CO can never be STRONGER; divergences are preserved for Step 3.

topic: Reported MUST accepted on knowledge-skill imperatives
evidence: FG-M-dcf938220d, FG-M-084304b42e, FG-M-a9131f9b4d: MUST from the reported label against DEFAULT policies
problem: The reported-consensus modality default could silently strengthen technique text.
interim_handling: Unmarked positive imperatives in knowledge skills and private references are DEFAULT unless the source says must, never or do not.

topic: No explicit source-quote verification status on records
evidence: M records held only the inherited Step-1 location_status per reference
problem: A reader could not tell from a record whether the cited text had been re-verified in this step.
interim_handling: Mechanical source_quote_verification on every record, with exact primary_quote and hash; a FAILED status blocks validation.

evidence: FG-M-1c4fc44b5e and 35 further normative records carried trigger UNKNOWN_NOT_REPORTED
problem: The field default copied the absence of a reported trigger as if it were attributed text, so source conditions could be lost.
interim_handling: trigger_status and exceptions_status are explicit; MISSING on a normative record blocks validation; later batches must state the condition at build time.

topic: Failed semantic challenge coexisted with a passing report
evidence: FG-M-22cae42396 stayed CANONICAL_ONLY/HIGH while its challenge said REVISED_NEEDED
problem: The validator did not connect challenge outcomes to record state.
interim_handling: Each challenge has a resolution; OPEN_UNRESOLVED is a validation error; samples are frozen so corrections cannot change what was challenged.

topic: Flat negatives on knowledge-skill and private-reference text
evidence: _decisions/A13_AUDIT_FINDINGS.jsonl category N (79 records), e.g. FG-M1-e1ac413363 'Not retried:', FG-K0-418eb178cc 'not a dumping ground'
problem: A1.3 names unmarked positive imperatives. It does not say how to read a flat negative such as 'no X', 'not X' or 'only when' with no must, never or do not.
interim_handling: Kept at the recorded MUST_NOT and listed in COVERAGE_LIMITATIONS.md. Definitions were not changed.

topic: Round-1 challenge pool drew no NON_NORMATIVE record in five candidates
evidence: candidate.py families(): the NN pool asked for HIGH confidence, and every NN record in M1, L0, L1, K0 and K1 is MEDIUM
problem: The task requires a challenge of NON_NORMATIVE classifications. The gate found that round 1 sampled none in those candidates.
interim_handling: Added a frozen round 2 of 5 NN records per candidate (25 in all), with the pool falling back to all NN records when none is HIGH. Round-1 samples were not changed.
